lead: From jewels of civil Gothic to contemporary art, by way of interactive science and Fallas tradition. Valencia’s culture unfolds across more than 60 cultural venues.

Valencia packs some of the Peninsula’s most singular monuments into its historic centre: a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Valencian Sistine Chapel, the best-preserved medieval wall in the Mediterranean and the largest Modernista market in Europe. All of it within a ten-minute walk.

On top of that there is a network of more than 34 museums, ranging from the second-largest art gallery in Spain to collections unique in the world devoted to Fallas ninots, toy lead soldiers and the silk industry.

items.title: La Lonja de la Seda
items.body: A masterpiece of 15th-century Valencian civil Gothic. Its helical columns, the Orange Tree Courtyard and the Consulate of the Sea Hall make it one of the most impressive buildings in Europe.

items.title: Valencia Cathedral and Miguelete
items.body: It houses the Holy Chalice, the relic that tradition identifies with the Grail. The Miguelete bell tower offers the best views of the historic centre from its height of 50 metres.
facts: Plaza de la Reina · Historic centre

items.title: Church of San Nicolás de Bari
items.body: A 14th-century Gothic church whose vaults are covered by almost 2,000 m² of 17th-century Baroque frescoes, the work of Antonio Palomino and Dionís Vidal. One of the most spectacular interiors in Spain.
facts: C/ de los Caballeros · Historic centre

items.title: Serranos Towers
items.body: The old north gate of the walled city. Built between 1392 and 1398, they are among the finest examples of Gothic military architecture in Europe. From their terraces, panoramic views of the Turia Gardens.
facts: Plaza de los Fueros · El Carmen district

items.title: Central Market
items.body: One of the largest food markets in Europe, with more than 250 stalls beneath a magnificent early 20th-century Modernista dome. The nerve centre of Valencian gastronomy.

items.title: City of Arts and Sciences
items.body: Valencia’s most iconic skyline: the Oceanogràfic, the Museu de les Ciències, the Hemisfèric and the Palau de les Arts, spread along the old Turia riverbed in an architectural ensemble without equal.
facts: Av. del Professor López Piñero · Turia
Open every day of the year

blocks.title: Tips for visiting museums and monuments
items: The València Tourist Card includes free admission to municipal museums and monuments
Most municipal museums are free all year round
San Nicolás requires advance booking — it sells out quickly at weekends
For the CAC it is best to buy tickets online to avoid queues
The Fine Arts Museum is free and opens Tuesday to Sunday
Most museums in the city close on Mondays
